_comment: experiment 1 arm n256: runs/prereg.jsonl#conversion_rate_0905 amendment 6, 500 steps, world 2, cards 5+7.

WEIGHTS ARE ROW-DERIVED, not token-derived (4c's ruling 2026-09-05). build_mix computes its budget as total_tokens/seq (4096) while a pool packs at seq+1 (4097), so a weight from a token count asks int(tok/4096) rows of a tok//4097-row pool and the epoch cap binds by one row at n8/n64/n256. Row-derived: want == pool exactly. The unit mismatch is build_mix's and is filed to be fixed AFTER both launches -- E1's control ran under the old arithmetic.
w_S = 0.2029687500 (20.2969% of the arm) = 6495 rows; w_P = 0.0006250000 = 20 rows; natural domains x 0.7964062034. S 26,611,200 tokens and P 84,434 both MEASURED.

Both injection domains carry val_frac: 0 (train.py's per-domain override, scripts/test_mix_val_frac.py). Without it the 5% split comes off the FRONT of the shard and the realised exposure count is 0.95n against an axis that says n.
The base mix's weights sum to 1.0000000585, not 1; the scale divides by that sum so this arm does not inherit the 5.85e-08 error.

p_format.role: P format control: 1000 documents, ONE exposure in EVERY arm including control_arm -- its count must not vary with n or a P movement could not be read. 84,434 tokens MEASURED with data/tokenizer.json (84.43/doc, NOT S's 104: the prereg's 104 is S_pool's mean and applying it here asked 25 rows of a 20-row pool). Weight = 20 packed rows / 32000 budget rows. val_frac 0.

s_inject_n256.role: S injection: 1000 documents x 256 exposure(s) = 26,611,200 tokens MEASURED, 6495 packed rows. Weight = 6495/32000 so want == pool exactly and the epoch cap never binds. epochs=1: the repeats are materialised in the shard by a seeded permutation, so epochs>1 would re-read it and multiply the exposure count under measurement. val_frac 0 so all 256 exposures of all 1000 documents reach training.
